title: canary rollout notes - maya singh
content:
Quick scratchpad for upcoming canary rollout (notes to self).

Context:
- Target change: model pin + kv-cache fix + batcher tweak (see PR 1286).
- Goal: roll new model variant (m-instruct-v2-quant) behind canary; preserve current prod as fallback.
- Risk: slightly higher p99 on long sequences after kernel swap, need to watch tail latency and cost.

Rollout strategy (high level):
- Nightly canary for 4h (low traffic) -> 1% of traffic next day (business hours) -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%
- Each step >= 60m steady-state and at least 500 requests or 10k tokens, whichever later.

Checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Confirm PR 1286 merged and image pushed (owner: Alex)
- [ ] Tag release artifact: serving-runtime:v2026-03-03-canary (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Update routing policy: route policy id = canary-model-2026-03 (Jordan)
- [ ] Pin model versions for fallback: prod -> m-instruct-v1 (immutable commit hash recorded)
- [ ] Smoke test: basic generation + long-seq generation (2000 tokens) on private cluster (Priya)
- [ ] Verify telemetry: datadog alerts, prometheus queries, SLO dashboards linked
- [ ] Postmortem template pre-created in Confluence (link above)

Canary steps (operational):
1) Deploy image to canary pool (gpu-pool-canary). Keep autoscale disabled.
2) Route 0.1% traffic for 60m. Observe latency, errors.
3) If green -> bump to 1% for 60m.
4) If green -> bump 5% -> 20% (each step wait 60m and min request count).
5) At each step run quick eval set (local harness) to check quality/regression. See linked eval job INF-4821.

Metrics to watch (primary):
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (generation token time)
- error rate (5xx, model runtime errors)
- cost per 1k tokens (estimate from billing probe)
- rollback triggers: p99 > baseline + 150ms for 30m OR error rate > 0.5% absolute increase
- quality: BLEU/ROUGE on eval set (quick eval) and classification accuracy on critical prompts

Rollforward criteria:
- No latency spikes beyond threshold at each step
- Error rate stable or improving
- Quick eval metrics within acceptable deltas (see INF-4821 thresholds)

Rollback plan:
- Immediate: reduce route to 0% and switch to prod model variant (m-instruct-v1)
- If automation fails: manual re-deploy using serving-runtime:v2026-02-20-prod and re-pin in routing config
- Post-rollback: collect heap/profile logs, request traces for failing requests (trace ids via tracing hook), open postmortem

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to confirm whether cache warm-up will cause a transient cost spike — add specific probe to track KV cache fill rate. (Action: Jordan)
- Can we run a background synthetic workload to pre-warm KV cache? Ops says maybe; check infra quotas.
- Where to record exact model commit hashes for audit? Confluence runbook + release artifact registry.

Notes from yesterday's run-through:
- Observed small p99 bump (~80ms) on 2048 token requests when using kernel A. Might be acceptable but need to quantify cost impact.
- Batch size tweak reduced GPU utilization variance; might help p95. Keep batcher config as batcher_v3 for canary.

Communication plan:
- Slack #release-updates: announce start + link to dashboard + expected windows
- Pager on-call if rollback triggers fire
- Post-rollout notes: short summary and next steps in Confluence and this doc (update this file)

Owner responsibilities:
- Maya: coordinate rollout and final sign-off at each stage
- Jordan: routing config + telemetry checks
- Alex: image build and infra rollout
- Priya: quality evals and smoke tests

Small reminders (notes-to-self):
- Keep increments conservative during business hours (no >20% step).
- Double-check commit hashes before final 100% sweep.
- If we see model hallucinations uptick, pause and run deeper evals.

Quick links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1286
- JIRA runbook: INF-4723, INF-4821
- Datadog: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/canary-inference-metrics

---
End of scratchpad. Will turn into a more formal runbook if we go past 20% without issues.
